notes.text: For more than 4, use two sheet pans, one on each middle rack, and swap them halfway.

move.title: Raw chicken, start to finish
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week: you handle raw chicken on your own, from the package to the plate, with an adult in the kitchen. The chicken comes ready-cut, so the work is keeping it away from everything else, baking it to 165°F, and tossing it in a sweet, shiny teriyaki glaze you make yourself.

why.title: Don't rinse it
why.body: Rinsing raw chicken doesn't clean it. It splashes germs onto the sink and counter. Baking it to 165°F is what makes it safe.

why.title: One spot for raw chicken
why.body: Keep the raw chicken, its package, and the bowl it's in in one spot. Anything that touches it gets washed before it touches anything else.

why.title: One layer, a little space
why.body: Chicken piled up steams and stays pale. Spread out in one layer, the hot air reaches every side, so it browns and cooks evenly.

why.title: Cornstarch thickens the glaze
why.body: Cornstarch stirred into cold liquid, then heated, turns clear and thick. That's what makes the glaze cling to the chicken.

why.title: Chicken is done at 165°F
why.body: All chicken needs 165°F in the thickest piece. Check two pieces, because some are always bigger.

wrong.fix: Microwave it 30 more seconds and stir. It thickens as it heats.
Stir in a spoonful of water.
Spread it out more next time so the pieces don't touch.
Bake 3 more minutes and check again.

steps.text: Clear a spot on the counter for the raw chicken. Set out the large bowl, the lined sheet pan, and the oil and salt.
steps.tip: This is the mastery check. Work through it yourself.

steps.text: Move a rack to the middle of the cold oven. Heat the oven to 425°F.
In the medium bowl, whisk the soy sauce, honey, water, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch until smooth.
steps.look: No lumps of cornstarch on the bottom.

steps.text: Tip the chicken into the large bowl. Don't rinse it. Stir in the oil and salt, then spoon it onto the pan in one layer.
steps.look: Pieces in one layer, not touching.
steps.tip: Put the package in the trash, and the spoon and bowl in the sink.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds. Wipe the counter where the chicken was with hot, soapy water.
Mitts on. Slide the pan into the oven and bake.
steps.look: White all over, golden at the edges.

steps.text: While it bakes, microwave the glaze, stirring every 30 seconds, until it bubbles and thickens.
steps.tip: Lift the bowl out with a mitt. It gets hot.

steps.text: Mitts on, pull the rack out. Check the two biggest pieces with the thermometer. Each should read 165°F or more.
steps.tip: Not there yet? Bake 3 more minutes.

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Scoop the chicken into the bowl of glaze with the spatula and stir to coat.
Heat the rice pouches in the microwave as the package says.
steps.tip: Tear the pouch open away from your face.

steps.text: Spoon the chicken over the rice. Sprinkle with sesame seeds if you're using them.
steps.look: Glossy brown bites on white rice.
